note: Literature directly reports that heterozygous nonsense (loss-of-function) SPTAN1 variants present with distal HMN and upper motor neuron signs.

evidence.text: Individuals carrying heterozygous nonsense variants in SPTAN1 exhibited hereditary motor neuropathy accompanied by mild upper motor neuron signs, contradicting the premise that loss-of-function variants spare the corticospinal tract.

evidence.text: Distal hereditary motor neuropathy caused by dominant SPTAN1 variants is characterized in the literature by upper motor neuron involvement.
